review.finding: The two registries (lib.review_payloads.CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_BASENAMES and the salvage hook's local CANONICAL_BASENAME mirror) were pinned to the same literals only one-sidedly, and no test exercised the hook's output feeding record_review_pass.py record -- the exact boundary the docstring promises.
review.suggestion: Add a test pinning both dicts equal, and a round-trip test: run the hook against a fixture transcript, then record_review_pass.main([...]) against its output, asserting exit 0.

review.finding: test_recording_a_marker_type_as_completed_requires_a_marker_status recorded --review-type external_code with CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_BASENAMES['plan'] -- passed only because marker-status validation runs before the basename check.
review.suggestion: Use CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_BASENAMES['external_code'] so the test isolates the marker-status rule.

review.finding: The usage error said the payload 'must be named ... under the run directory', but canonical_basename_error compares the basename only -- the parent directory is never checked, so the message overclaimed what is enforced.
review.suggestion: Drop 'under the run directory' from the message; note the directory half as a documented boundary instead of enforcing it (out of this change's proportionate scope).

review.finding: Prose examples were inconsistent about the path prefix: some gave a relative '.shipwright/planning/iterate/{run_id}/...' path while others gave '{project_root}/...' -- a real cwd-resolution hazard for --payload-file, especially for the campaign orchestrator.
review.suggestion: Prefix every example with '{project_root}/' so all four docs agree.

review.finding: The table footer states the table must always restate CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_BASENAMES verbatim, but nothing enforced that -- the prose table is the artifact agents actually read at runtime, so it is the more likely of the two to drift.
review.suggestion: Add a test that reads iteration-reviews.md by path and asserts every CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_BASENAMES value appears in it.
